subject: general
question:
**Fill in the blank:**

Ladakhhi new year (Losar) is welcomed with symbolic dough models of ______, sun, and moon placed in households.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ibex**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In Ladakh, the Losar festival marks the beginning of the Tibetan New Year and holds great cultural and spiritual importance.
 
• The symbolic dough models of ibex, sun, and moon are placed in households as a part of the Losar celebrations to bring prosperity and well-being.
 
• The ibex is considered a sacred and auspicious animal in Ladakh, symbolizing strength, resilience, and endurance.
 
• These dough models are not only decorative but also carry spiritual significance, serving as offerings to deities and a representation of harmony with nature.
 
• Losar is celebrated with rituals, prayers, and traditional performances, reflecting the rich heritage of Tibetan Buddhism practiced in Ladakh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Yak**

 
 
• The yak is a domesticated bovine animal found in the Himalayan region, including Ladakh, and is vital for the livelihood of the locals.
 
• Yaks provide milk, meat, wool, and transportation, making them indispensable in high-altitude areas.
 
• Although important in Ladakhi culture, the yak does not hold the same symbolic or spiritual significance as the ibex during Losar celebrations.
 
 
 
• **Snow Leopard**
 
 
• The snow leopard is a rare and endangered species found in the mountainous regions of Ladakh.
 
• It holds ecological importance as a top predator in the Himalayan ecosystem and is a symbol of Ladakh's wildlife diversity.
 
• However, it does not feature in the symbolic representations of the Losar festival.
 
 
 
• **Buddha**
 
 
• Buddha is a revered spiritual figure in Tibetan Buddhism, which is widely practiced in Ladakh.
 
• While Buddhist rituals and prayers play a key role during Losar, the symbolic dough models do not traditionally include representations of Buddha.
 
 
 
• **Losar Festival**
 
 
• Losar is celebrated during the 11th month of the Tibetan calendar, usually falling in December or January.
 
• The festival includes cleaning homes, lighting lamps, and performing traditional dances and songs to welcome the new year.
 
• It emphasizes harmony, renewal, and gratitude towards nature and deities.
